subject: Staged evaluation milestones, surge policy & ramp caps
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@nimbushealth.com>, Alex Cortez <alex.cortez@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Draft MAP and surge policy for staged evaluation

Hi Sara / Alex —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP_Nimbus_Draft_v2.pdf) and a simplified rate card extract (rate_card_nimbus_v1.xlsx). Key points I wanted to call out up front:

- Evaluation plan: 6-week staged evaluation with 3 milestone gates (POC ingestion, clinical integration, pilot throughput), each tied to an acceptance checklist in the MAP.
- Committed baseline: Nimbus would commit to a 3-month reserve starting at pilot close; during the evaluation we propose a small non-binding usage target so the onboarding team can size capacity.
- Surge (overage) policy for ramp: to avoid surprise bills during the ramp, we propose a capped surge allowance for the evaluation window — see section 3 of the MAP for the mechanics.

Before we finalize language, can you confirm the expected peak qps/token profile for weeks 3–6 and whether nursing staff or batch jobs will generate bursty traffic? That will help Ben size the recommended cap.

Attached: MAP draft (PDF), simplified rate card (XLSX), and a sample usage graph.

Next steps I suggest:
1) You review the MAP and rate card and mark any redlines.
2) We align on a capped surge allowance for the evaluation period (I put a placeholder in the doc).
3) If that works, we update the commercial appendix and route for legal/finance review.

Happy to hop on a short call if you prefer to walk through the ramp mechanics.

Best,
Michael Grant
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

On attachments: MAP_Nimbus_Draft_v2.pdf (PDF, 42 KB); rate_card_nimbus_v1.xlsx (XLSX, 18 KB); sample-usage-graph.png (PNG, 120 KB)
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@nimbushealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-13T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP and surge policy for staged evaluation

Thanks Michael — useful outline. A few clarifying questions before we share with procurement: 

1) What do you mean by 'capped surge allowance'? Is that a hard token cap during the evaluation, or a softer discount on overage pricing?
2) How will overage be billed if we exceed the cap — do you bill at list rate or an accelerated surcharge?
3) We need to understand whether any burst above the cap will affect our eligibility for the pilot pricing at commit.

For context: our pilot week often sees a 2–3x spike from scheduled nightly ingest jobs in addition to clinician sessions. If the cap is set too low we'll hit it quickly.

If you can outline an example invoice scenario (baseline + 2x burst for 48 hours) that would help our procurement and finance team sign off.

Thanks,
Sara
Head of Platform Integrations
Nimbus Health
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-14T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP and surge policy for staged evaluation

Hi Sara — great questions. Below is a concise example and the proposed commercial mechanics we typically use for staged evaluations: 

1) What is a 'capped surge allowance'?
   - For the evaluation window we propose a soft capped allowance: a specified token allowance above the stated baseline where overage is billed at a reduced evaluation overage rate (not list). It's intended to absorb predictable spikes during onboarding without immediate full-rate billing. The MAP draft includes the placeholder: "Evaluation surge allowance = up to 150% of baseline per 24h, billed at $0.009/token overage rate (capped to $X/day)".

2) Billing if you exceed the cap
   - If usage exceeds the evaluation surge allowance, standard rate-card overage applies. Example tiers:
     - Within allowance: billed at reduced eval overage price ($0.009/token)
     - Above allowance: billed at standard overage ($0.013/token)
   - We can also add a daily hard cap (maximum daily overage bill) for the evaluation phase to limit your financial exposure; suggested default = $2,500/day for this pilot (can be adjusted).

3) Effect on pilot pricing eligibility
   - We will not penalize you on eligibility for pilot-to-commit pricing if usage in the evaluation phase is within the MAP-defined allowance or within a single-day hard-cap exception. Repeated large overages outside the MAP may trigger re-sizing conversations but would not automatically void the pilot pricing unless there is prolonged sustained usage beyond agreed thresholds.

Illustrative invoice scenario (numbers simplified):
- Baseline committed during evaluation: 1M tokens/day at pilot baseline rate (pre-commit)
- 48-hour incident: average 2x tokens/day for two days = additional 2M tokens over 48h
- Of those 2M extra tokens: first 1M fall within evaluation surge allowance (billed at $0.009/token) = $9,000
- Remaining 1M billed at standard overage $0.013/token = $13,000, but subject to daily hard cap (so we would cap to $2,500/day if that clause is enacted)

Ben — can you confirm we can commit to the $0.009 eval overage line and a $2,500/day hard cap for Nimbus? Laura — is finance comfortable with the proposed example wording so procurement can sign off?

Michael
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP and surge policy for staged evaluation

On Fri, Oct 14, 2025 at 08:28 Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ben — can you confirm we can commit to the $0.009 eval overage line and a $2,500/day hard cap for Nimbus? Laura — is finance comfortable with the proposed example wording so procurement can sign off?

Michael — technically that pricing is OK for the evaluation window if we limit it to the 6-week staged MAP and require telemetry hooks that allow auto-throttling when KV/cache thresholds approach limits. Two small asks from my side:
1) Add a clause that scheduled batch ingests must be identified in the MAP schedule so we can pre-warm caches; otherwise bursts may degrade latency and invalidate the assumed cost model.
2) Include a one-time onboarding buffer credit (we usually do a $5k one-off credit for enterprise pilots) to cover unexpected early tuning and token explosions.

Laura — can you confirm finance on the hard-cap exposure?

—Ben

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sara Lim <sara.lim@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2025-10-20T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP and surge policy for staged evaluation

Hi all — quick finance note and next steps: 

- Finance is comfortable with the $0.009 eval overage rate and a $2,500/day hard cap for the 6-week evaluation provided we add a maximum aggregate cap for the entire evaluation period (recommendation: $25k total overage exposure). That protects both parties and is straightforward for procurement to accept.
- We support Ben's ask to surface scheduled batch ingest windows in the MAP and will add an onboarding buffer credit of $5,000 to the commercial appendix.

Sara — if that aligns with Nimbus, I can prepare the commercial appendix update and a clean MAP for signature. I will include:
  * Evaluation surge allowance: up to 150% baseline/day at $0.009/token (first line of overage)
  * Standard overage above allowance: $0.013/token
  * Daily hard cap: $2,500/day
  * Aggregate evaluation overage cap: $25,000 total
  * One-time onboarding credit: $5,000 applied to first invoice

If you confirm, I will drop the updated appendix into the shared MAP link and trigger the DocuSign envelope.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
VP, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

On attachments: updated commercial appendix to follow as PDF stub when ready.
